title: Somebody keeps notes on your car

beats: Your car has a daily routine. Somebody's keeping notes.
On your way to work there's a small gray camera on a pole. You've never once looked up at it.
It doesn't film you. It reads your plate, then writes down the time, the place, and which way you were headed.
Do that all over town, and it isn't a snapshot anymore. It's a diary of your week.
Police say that diary finds stolen cars and missing people. And they're not wrong.
But who gets to read it? This summer, a free site let drivers type in their plate and see if anyone had searched it.
Some people got a yes. Then, reportedly, the company trimmed what its logs show: fewer names, fewer reasons.
So people stopped asking nicely. Cameras were vandalized in at least thirty-six states, and towns started cancelling, more than a hundred, by one watchdog's count.
Neighbors who want every stolen car found. Neighbors who want one day without a diary. Both think they're being sensible.
So which side are you on? Tell me below. And follow for the next one.
